Filed by the `domain:ui` execution seat (Seat: domain:ui#2, session `session_018HrVaotisyhgmot9o2MLRq`) while accepting PR objectui#10161 for objectui#10120. ⛔ Filed bare: `domain:*`, `priority:*` and `type` are the triage seat's production.

⚠️ Cited by content rather than by line address, per AGENTS.md #11.

## The finding

The child-row grid inside a master-detail form consults **no field-level permission** when deciding which cells are editable. It reads only `schema.readonly` for `allow_add` / `allow_delete` and passes that same flag down to the cells.

⇒ a field the caller's permission set marks `editable: false` renders as a **live, editable cell** in the line-items grid, on the same page where objectui#10120 has just taught the surrounding form to disable it.

## Why it is filed, and what it is NOT

This is the **same affordance class as objectui#10120's second clause, one container over.** That card's boundary was the record edit form and its three containers; PR objectui#10161 unified them onto one render pass and one outbound filter. The line-items grid was outside that boundary and stayed on its own answer — which is exactly the shape objectui#10120 was about: ⭐ **a family where each container spells its own copy of the gate, and the one that carries no copy is where the user gets bitten.**

⚠️ **The outbound half is partly covered already** and this card ⛔ must not be read as claiming a live 403: a master-detail child update sends only the cells that differ from the loaded snapshot (landed in PR objectui#10154), so an untouched FLS-denied column is not resent. What remains is the **affordance** — the UI invites an edit the server will refuse. ⭐ A refusal the UI invites is worse than a refusal it prevents, which is the reasoning objectui#10120's own second clause rests on.

## ⛔ Measured by neither this seat nor on this branch

Relayed from the PR objectui#10161 dev's report, which names it as out of scope for that card and explicitly did **not** measure it on its branch. ⛔ This seat re-derived none of it. Step 1 for whoever takes this: reproduce with the card's sibling fixture — a permission set marking one child column `readable: true, editable: false` — and establish with a **lit control** that a non-denied column in the same grid stays editable, so the finding is a difference rather than an absence.

## The shape of the fix, when graded

⭐ Read PR objectui#10161's landed diff first and **reuse**, ⛔ do not re-implement: `checkField(object, field, 'write')` in `@object-ui/permissions` is the one 「may this caller edit this field」 answer, `fieldWriteGate` adapts it into a predicate, and `applyFieldPermissions` is the single render pass the three form containers now share. The correct fix is very likely to route this grid through that same pass — ⛔ a fourth copy of the gate is the defect this family keeps reproducing.

⚠️ Preserve the fail-open-with-no-provider behaviour that PR objectui#10161 kept unchanged; ⛔ it is not this card's to move.

## Dedupe words

`LineItemsPanel field permissions editable cell` · `line items child rows FLS affordance` · `master-detail grid schema.readonly allow_add` · `objectui#10120 clause 2 one container over` · `checkField write child grid`
